findings.description: The sync wrapper sets `copy._local.statistics = self._local.statistics` rather than the shared `stats` dict. `self._local.statistics` is only reassigned on the next line, so the copy gets whatever `self._local.statistics` held before, not the dict that was just cleared.
findings.rationale: Trigger: any call to a function decorated with @retry. `copy._local.statistics` is bound to the old `self._local.statistics`, which is either a different dict or absent in this thread. The copy's retry state (attempt_number, etc.) then never lands in `wrapped_f.statistics`, so that dict stays empty after `stats.clear()`. Users reading `f.statistics` see `{}`. If the thread-local has no `statistics` attribute yet, this raises AttributeError. The async version correctly uses `stats`.
